findings.title: Orchestrator-side rejection of invalid add-in messages has no valid wire error contract
findings.location: Section 5 "ToolResultMessage envelope invariant"; Section 6.3 "Message-level enums"; Section 9 "AddinSessionId and Epoch"
findings.evidence: Section 5: "Receivers MUST reject invalid envelopes with `AddinProtocolErrorCode.MalformedEnvelope`." Section 9: "All non-`AddinReadyMessage` messages received before the first epoch is established MUST be rejected with `AddinProtocolErrorCode.StaleEpoch`." and "any non-`AddinReadyMessage` with an `AddinSessionId` other than the current epoch is rejected with `AddinProtocolErrorMessage(ErrorCode: StaleEpoch)`." Section 6.3 defines `ClientProtocolErrorCode` as only `VersionMismatch`, `MessageTooLarge`, `UnknownMessageType`.
findings.problem: The receiver for `ToolResultMessage`, `StateUpdateMessage`, and stale-epoch add-in traffic is the orchestrator, but the spec routes those failures through `AddinProtocolErrorMessage` / `AddinProtocolErrorCode`, which are add-in→orchestrator types. There is no `IClientMessage` error code for `StaleEpoch` or `MalformedEnvelope`, so the orchestrator cannot implement the required rejection behavior.
findings.why_it_matters: This breaks implementation of core validation paths and will force ad hoc close/discard behavior that other specs cannot rely on or test.
findings.proposed_fix: Add orchestrator-emittable error semantics for inbound add-in validation failures (`StaleEpoch`, `MalformedEnvelope`, and any other add-in-side parse/validation failures), or explicitly specify that these cases are connection-close-only with no protocol message. Update the enums, message definitions, and required tests to match one directionally consistent contract.

findings.title: The 4 MiB message cap conflicts with the mandatory full-state snapshot contract
findings.evidence: Section 3: "Maximum single-message size: 4 MiB." and producers should reduce payloads "e.g., `GetFeatureTreeInput` with depth limits, or omitting suppressed features." Section 5 defines `StateUpdateMessage` with required `StateSnapshot State`. `StateUpdateTrigger.InitialState` is documented as "Post-handshake full-state resync (mandatory after AddinReady)". Section 8 makes `StateSnapshot.FeatureTree` required. Section 7.1 `GetFeatureTreeInput` only contains `IncludeSuppressed`.
findings.problem: The spec requires an initial full-state resync that always includes a `FeatureTree`, but it defines no truncation, pagination, or depth-limit fields for `StateSnapshot`, and the cited `GetFeatureTreeInput` depth-limit example does not exist in the contract.
findings.why_it_matters: Large models can make the mandatory initial snapshot impossible to send without violating either completeness or the 4 MiB limit, causing connection failures or undocumented producer-side omission behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Define an explicit large-state contract before implementation: pagination, truncation flags plus follow-up fetch API, or a separate lightweight initial snapshot that omits/full-loads the feature tree by negotiated policy. Remove the nonexistent "depth limits" example unless the fields are added.

findings.title: Placeholder stretch tools are exposed as real tools with no executable contract
findings.location: Section 7.2 "Stretch Tools"; Section 11 "Tool Registry and Schema Generation"; Section 17 "Consumption by Other Specs"
findings.evidence: Section 7.2: "These are empty placeholder records ... Their polymorphic registrations (`[JsonDerivedType]` on `IToolInput`/`IToolResult`) and `[ToolName]` attributes are present from day one so that `ToolRegistry` and completeness tests remain valid." Section 11: "`ToolRegistry.All` reflects the Protocol assembly at static construction time, finding every type with `[ToolName]` attributes..." Section 17: "SPEC-05 imports `ToolRegistry`."
findings.problem: The registry and generated schemas will treat stretch placeholders as callable tools even though their inputs/results are empty TODO shells and runtime behavior is deferred.
findings.why_it_matters: Consumers that build tool catalogs from `ToolRegistry` or generated schemas can advertise or invoke tools that have no implementable behavior, creating integration churn and runtime failures that tests in this spec will not catch.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an explicit implementation-status flag to `ToolMetadata` and exclude non-implemented tools from `ToolRegistry.All`/schema generation, or keep placeholders out of the runtime registry until their wire contracts are defined.

findings.title: Hash-ordering rules contradict the property-test requirement for reordered arrays
findings.evidence: Section 13 says: "Arrays are hashed in their serialized order. Producers MUST emit arrays in canonical order..." The same section says: "Property-based tests (`HashCanonicalization_PropertyTests` via FsCheck) generate 1000 randomly shaped `FeatureNode` trees and assert that logical equality (including reordered-but-equivalent arrays) implies hash equality."
findings.problem: If arrays are hashed in serialized order, reordered arrays cannot hash equally unless `HashCanonicalizer` sorts them internally. The spec simultaneously assigns ordering responsibility to producers and expects the canonicalizer/tests to erase ordering differences.
findings.why_it_matters: Different implementations will place sorting in different layers, producing inconsistent hashes and nondeterministic test behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one contract: either `HashCanonicalizer` sorts all hashed arrays itself, or producers must pre-sort and reordered arrays must produce different hashes. Then align the text and tests to that single rule.

findings.title: WebSocket framing guidance contradicts actual receive-loop behavior
findings.evidence: Section 3 states both: "Receivers MUST accumulate frames until `EndOfMessage = true` before deserializing." and "`System.Net.WebSockets` handles frame reassembly transparently; application code never sees partial frames."
findings.problem: These statements conflict. In `System.Net.WebSockets`, application code does receive partial segments and must loop until `EndOfMessage` is true.
findings.why_it_matters: Implementers following the second sentence will write incorrect readers and false-positive tests around framing behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the "handles frame reassembly transparently" claim and replace it with an explicit receive-loop contract stating that partial segments are expected and must be accumulated until `EndOfMessage`.

findings.title: `StateSnapshot` leaves document-present and sketch-active invariants undefined
findings.evidence: Section 8 defines null-document rules only for `IsNullDocumentState == true`, plus one inverse rule: "When `IsNullDocumentState` is `false`, `Units` MUST be non-null." The record still allows nullable `DocumentId`, `DocumentName`, `DocumentType`, and `ActiveSketchId` with no stated inverse invariants.
findings.problem: The contract permits internally inconsistent snapshots such as `IsNullDocumentState=false` with `DocumentId=null`, or `IsSketchActive=false` with a non-null `ActiveSketchId`, because those cases are not prohibited by the stated rules.
findings.why_it_matters: Consumers cannot reliably reason about state presence, and validators/tests have no complete basis for rejecting inconsistent snapshots.
findings.proposed_fix: Add inverse invariants for document-present state and sketch state (for example, document identifiers/type required when `IsNullDocumentState=false`, `ActiveSketchId` required iff `IsSketchActive=true`, forbidden otherwise) and make them build-breaking validator/test requirements.

top_3_must_fix: Define a directionally valid error contract for orchestrator rejection of invalid/stale add-in messages.
Resolve the 4 MiB limit versus mandatory full `StateSnapshot`/`FeatureTree` by adding an explicit large-state transfer contract.
Stop exposing empty stretch placeholders as runtime tools unless the registry/schema can mark them unavailable.
